messages:
Anya Patel: Quick summary from the Tempest30b bring-up across regions + GPUs. Ran FP16/BF16, FP8 (mma_fp8), and INT8 (cutlass_int8) profiles on us-west-2 (L40s), eu-west-1 (GH200), ap-southeast-1 (H100). TL;DR: INT8 gives the largest throughput wins (2.9-3.2x) with small but measurable quality deltas on abstractive summarization; FP8 is a sweet spot for us — ~2.0x speedup with ~0.1% quality change. Full CSV + traces: https://internal-redwood/bench/tempest30b/2275019001/results.csv :chart_with_upwards_trend:

benchbot: Automated summary attached. Parsed metrics:
- baseline FP16 (B=1, seq=1024)
  - GH200 (eu-west-1): 540 tok/s, p50=52ms, p95=170ms
  - H100 (ap-southeast-1): 450 tok/s, p50=62ms, p95=210ms
  - L40s (us-west-2): 410 tok/s, p50=68ms, p95=230ms
- FP8 (mma_fp8)
  - GH200: 1150 tok/s (+2.1x), p50=25ms
  - H100: 980 tok/s (+2.17x), p50=30ms
  - L40s: 880 tok/s (+2.15x), p50=33ms
- INT8 (cutlass_int8, per-channel asymmetric)
  - GH200: 1700 tok/s (+3.15x), p50=12ms
  - H100: 1400 tok/s (+3.11x), p50=14ms
  - L40s: 1250 tok/s (+3.05x), p50=16ms

Liam Chen: Nice. What batch / concurrency were these measured at?

Anya Patel: Single-request (B=1) concurrency=1 for p50/p95. For throughput runs we saturate with async batches up to 64 inflight and measure tokens/sec steady-state. Seq=1024 for all runs.

Sanjay Rao: How did you do the quality evals? numbers for ROUGE / ppl?

Anya Patel: Eval harness = 100-prompt summarization set (internal news+docs mix). Deterministic sampling (top_p=0.0 greedy) to isolate numeric regressions. Metrics: avg ROUGE-L and perplexity on held-out stream. Delta vs FP16 baseline:
- FP8: ROUGE-L change -0.08% (stdev 0.12), ppl change +0.2%
- INT8: ROUGE-L change -0.95% (stdev 0.6), ppl change +1.1%
Also flagged 3 prompts where INT8 produced hallucinated factual dates (manual inspection).

Devon Park: Are the INT8 regressions consistent across GPUs/regions or noisy?

Anya Patel: Mostly consistent magnitude; GH200 had slightly better quality stability (fewer outliers) vs L40s/H100. Hypothesis: GH200 int8 kernels use per-tensor scaling fallback on attention heads weights where our per-channel quant had rare saturation — will dig in.

Sanjay Rao: Kernel choice details? we have multiple int8 kernels in runtime. Which ones did you pick?

Anya Patel: Ran two INT8 kernel variants: default cutlass_int8_fast (max perf) and cutlass_int8_stable (extra rescale clamps). Results shown above are cutlass_int8_fast. cutlass_int8_stable reduces speed by ~8-12% but improves ROUGE delta to -0.6% avg and removes 2 of the 3 hallucination cases.

Anya Patel: Serving config snippet we used:
```
model: tempest30b
quant_profiles:
  - name: fp8_mma_moderate
    kernels: [mma_fp8]
    fallback: fp16
  - name: int8_cutlass_fast
    kernels: [cutlass_int8_fast]
    fallback: fp16
batching:
  max_batch_size: 32
  async_inflight: 64
region_policy:
  us-west-2: prefer_l40s
  eu-west-1: prefer_gh200
  ap-southeast-1: prefer_h100
```

Liam Chen: Memory/kv-cache impact? INT8 should shrink activation memory right? numbers?

benchbot: Measured KV+activations memory (seq=1024, B=1):
- FP16 baseline: 46GB
- FP8: 36GB (~22% reduction)
- INT8: 30GB (~34% reduction)
This allowed +20% denser packing on GH200 when using INT8 (fewer nodes for same capacity).

Devon Park: For capacity planning, what's tokens/sec per node (1 GPU) at steady-state for a mixed workload (avg seq=512, B variable)?

Anya Patel: Ballpark (mixed short/med lenses, 60/40 split, async inflight 48):
- GH200 FP16: ~680 tok/s/node
- GH200 FP8: ~1450 tok/s/node
- GH200 INT8: ~2100 tok/s/node
Note: those are sustained tokens/sec measured with our request-replay tool (10k reqs). For latency-sensitive SLOs we recommend FP8 or FP16; INT8 is great for batchy/throughput tiers.

infra-bot: Observability note: enabling cutlass_int8_fast requires enabling kernel logging level WARN->INFO for one hour during rollout to catch quant saturation warnings. Schedule that during low-traffic window.

Sanjay Rao: Any reproducible artifacts to reproduce the bad prompts? we should add to regression suite if INT8 is used in prod.

Anya Patel: Yes, added 5 repro prompts to eval/regressions repo: https://internal-redwood/evals/tempest30b/int8_regressors.md. Will open PR to block int8 on canary if new model fails >1% ROUGE-L delta or produces >2 hallucinations per 100 prompts.

Liam Chen: For region fallback routing — if GH200 capacity constrained, do we route to H100 INT8 variants or fallback to FP8 on GH200?

Anya Patel: Policy we tested: prefer same-precision fallback chain: int8_cutlass_fast -> int8_cutlass_stable -> fp8_mma_moderate -> fp16. That keeps performance but avoids quality cliffs. We also observed cross-region hop adds ~20-35ms tail lat on real traffic (due to network), so routing policy accounts for latency SLOs.

Devon Park: Recommendation for product: ship FP8 by default for tempest30b, reserve INT8 for Dedicated/throughput tiers with stricter eval gates. FP8 gives ~2x perf with near-zero quality delta and predictable latency.

Anya Patel: Agreed. I'll prepare a rollout plan: (1) GA FP8 across hosted regions next week (staged canary 1%->10%->50%), (2) enable INT8 as opt-in in Dedicated with regression gate + manual review. Will post the rollout doc + timeline in #eng-releases. :white_check_mark:

benchbot: Logged follow-ups: issue#4721 (add int8 prompts to regression), task#4722 (enable kernel logging during canary), doc#4723 (rollout plan).

infra-bot: If anyone wants the raw perf traces or perf flamegraphs, ping infra-bench and I'll attach S3 links.

Anya Patel: Thanks all — will iterate on cutlass_int8_stable to try and close the remaining regressions before we enable wide Dedicated opt-in.
